newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian T-bills seen yielding 68-80 pct.
newsitem.headline: Russian T-bills seen yielding 68-80 pct.

text.p: An issue of Russian six-month Treasury bills is likely to yield between 68 and 80 percent on Wednesday, dealers said.
A new tranche of government bonds could yield 81-82 percent, they said.

The Finance Ministry auctions 7.50 trillion roubles of six-month GKO discount T-bills (series 22049) and 3.50 trillion roubles in a new tranche of 18-month OFZ interest-bearing government bonds (24003)

It also repays about 6.5 trillion roubles in maturing six-month T-bills (22024), pays about 820 billion roubles in interest on the two-year OFZ bond maturing March 1998 (24007) and offers 1 trillion roubles of one-year OGSZ savings bonds.
The average yield fell on Tuesday to 62 percent from 65.3 percent on Monday. Volume rose to 4.52 trillion roubles from 2.51 trillion.
Dealers said prices of long and medium-term issues rose and those of short issues either fell or were steady.
"Today's deals, in which there was a lot of money, created a mood on the market for a rise in prices tomorrow," said Most-Bank dealer Konstantin Bazarkin.
MFK dealer Denis Nechayev said the ministry would do all it could to place the T-bills with as low a yield as possible.
